place.source_title: St. Charles Hospital, 400 East New York Street

brief: Six-storey Art Deco Catholic hospital of 1932: buff brick with stepped vertical piers, a taller central tower block over the main entrance, flat roofs, and lower wings running back from the front. Parking lot and a lawn with a statue by the entrance; the emergency entrance is on the side street.

facade.notes: the former St. Charles Hospital (Aurora IL, 1932): a six-storey buff-brick Art Deco block with vertical piers, a taller central tower with stepped parapets over the entrance, stone spandrels; landscaped corner lawn with a row of columnar trees; now apartments

why.note: 1930s institutional Art Deco: vertical piers and setbacks
an old hospital reused as housing
